claims.text: The proposed intervention combines high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation.
Integrating these three methods can improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The integrated approach will improve determination of fusion enthalpy.
The integrated approach will improve determination of fusion entropy.
The integrated approach will improve determination of the volume change at the transition.
The integrated approach will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
The integrated approach will improve accuracy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The integrated approach will improve representation of thermodynamic effects relevant to the transition.
The integrated approach will adequately treat both solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
Phase transitions and thermodynamic properties serve as the structural mediator between the intervention and its outcomes.
The intervention is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy materials in high-temperature states.
The intervention remains applicable across relevant compositions and temperatures.
The complexity of multicomponent systems limits the proposed approach.
The need for extensive ab initio molecular dynamics limits the proposed approach.
The proposed approach can be benchmarked against existing methods using transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
